hidden_dual_route_1.name: {name}
hidden_dual_route_1.text: *In the end, what stays with me isn't just one person's voice. The envelope from the classroom and the bandage on the back of my hand come to mind at the same time.*

hidden_dual_route_choice.name: {name}
hidden_dual_route_choice.text: *This time, I have to decide that too.*
choices: Go to the person who handed me the manuscript
Go to the person who left an answer on the back of my hand

perfect_seo_1.name: {name}
perfect_seo_1.text: *Seoyeon's rooftop. Standing among the plants she grew herself.*

perfect_seo_1_b.name: {name}
perfect_seo_1_b.text: *She's crying again. Not in the bathroom — this time, right in front of me.*

perfect_seo_2.name: {name}
perfect_seo_2.text: *Her eyes are completely wet. Even so, she doesn't look away.*

perfect_seo_3.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_3.text: ...This face — only you get to see it.

perfect_seo_4.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_4.text: *The rooftop breeze stirs around us.* Even after graduation, I'll keep coming here. These plants only really grow when you're here.

perfect_seo_5.name: {name}
perfect_seo_5.text: *Seoyeon reaches out. Not a pinky finger. Her whole hand.*

perfect_epilogue_1_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_seo.text: *I walked the same road every morning. It wasn't five days — every moment beside Seoyeon was everything.*

perfect_epilogue_2_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_seo.text: *University entrance ceremony day. A message on my phone. 'Watered the plant today. — But come home soon.'*

perfect_epilogue_3_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_3_seo.text: *Seoyeon has changed. She knows she doesn't have to be perfect anymore. She smiles more now without checking the mirror first.*

bitter_seo_1.name: {name}
bitter_seo_1.text: *I confessed. Seoyeon said, 'Let's try.' But even the way she said okay sounded uncertain. About a month later, I got a message asking me to meet her at the cafe in front of the school.*

bitter_seo_2.name: Seoyeon
bitter_seo_2.text: ...I thought we'd make it work. We were both just one step short, I guess.

bitter_seo_2_b.name: {name}
bitter_seo_2_b.text: *Seoyeon at the cafe. Her gaze behind the glasses is dry. No composure, no trembling. Just — the eyes of someone who came to wrap things up.*

bitter_seo_3.name: {name}
bitter_seo_3.text: *I left the cafe. It's raining. We used to share one umbrella — now we each have our own.*

true_seo_1.name: {name}
true_seo_1.text: *Seoyeon's room. Her parents are out. The room is tidy — too tidy. The kind of tidy that feels hollow.*

true_seo_2.name: {name}
true_seo_2.text: *— Except for one thing. On the desk, a row of plants Seoyeon grew herself.*

true_seo_3.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_3.text: With you, I feel like I don't have to be perfect.

true_seo_4.name: {name}
true_seo_4.text: You never had to be perfect.

true_seo_5.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_5.text: ...I know. But it took five days to believe that.

true_seo_6.name: {name}
true_seo_6.text: *Seoyeon smiles. Her lips curve on their own.*

true_seo_6b.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_6b.text: I always had to smile. With you, I just want to be myself.

true_seo_7_b.name: {name}
true_seo_7_b.text: *Seoyeon hesitates, then holds out her pinky.*

true_seo_7b.name: {name}
true_seo_7b.text: *I reach out too. Just before our fingers touch, Seoyeon smiles first.*

true_seo_8.name: {name}
true_seo_8.text: *We linked pinkies. Day 1’s habit, Day 4’s promise, and now. — Same finger, third meaning.*

true_seo_bridge.name: {name}
true_seo_bridge.text: *Seoyeon's promise still lingers at my fingertips.*

true_epilogue_1_seo.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_seo.text: *It was five days. Five days to see the real person hiding behind Seoyeon's perfection.*

perfect_yuna_1.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_1.text: *The library annex, the secret attic. Yuna hands over a short story.*

perfect_yuna_2.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_2.text: *The title is the main character's name.*

perfect_yuna_3.name: Yuna
perfect_yuna_3.text: ...Tell me what you think after you finish it. That's my answer.

perfect_yuna_4.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_4.text: *The last line of the story: 'There was someone who never disappeared. Because of that person, I decided not to disappear either.'*

perfect_yuna_5.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_5.text: *Yuna stood up and wrapped her arms around me. Without a word. Moonlight poured through the broken windows — tattooed arms wrapped around my waist, silver hair resting on my shoulder. For the first time, Yuna's quiet breathing filled the hideout.*

perfect_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *I sat in the same seat every day. It wasn't five days — every silence shared with Yuna was everything.*

perfect_epilogue_2_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_yuna.text: *Yuna's debut novel was published. The dedication: 'To the third star.'*

perfect_epilogue_3_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_3_yuna.text: *Yuna still doesn't talk much. But her sentences are longer now. At least with me.*

bitter_yuna_1.name: {name}
bitter_yuna_1.text: *I confessed. Yuna nodded. But that nod felt more like trying than certainty. About a month later, a note appeared in my locker. 'Let's talk.'*

bitter_yuna_2.name: Yuna
bitter_yuna_2.text: ...Sometimes I think of you. When I catch the scent of old books. I should've said more back then.

bitter_yuna_3.name: {name}
bitter_yuna_3.text: *I walked out the school gate. It's raining. Yuna's last note is tucked in the mailbox. Short, as always. But this time it isn't brevity. There's simply nothing left to say.*

true_yuna_1.name: {name}
true_yuna_1.text: *The library annex. Deeper than the secret reading spot — an attic. A space I didn’t even know existed.*

true_yuna_2.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2.text: I was the only one who knew about this place.

true_yuna_2_b.name: {name}
true_yuna_2_b.text: *Yuna climbs the small attic ladder. There's a hatch leading up. — When it opens, a breeze rushes in.*

true_yuna_2_c.name: {name}
true_yuna_2_c.text: *Above the attic was the library annex rooftop. A secret passage no one else knows about.*

true_yuna_2_d.name: {name}
true_yuna_2_d.text: *Yuna leans against the railing. Stars are visible.*

true_yuna_3.name: {name}
true_yuna_3.text: *Yuna opens the small window. Stars are visible.*

true_yuna_5_b.name: {name}
true_yuna_5_b.text: *Yuna pauses. — Smiles. A soundless smile I've never seen before.*

true_yuna_7.name: {name}
true_yuna_7.text: *Day 2’s riddle. The third star. — Proof that Yuna had been watching me from the very beginning.*

true_yuna_bridge.name: {name}
true_yuna_bridge.text: *Yuna's stars are still here, right in front of me.*

true_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *It was five days. Five days to learn to read the words hidden inside Yuna's silence.*

perfect_dain_1.name: {name}
perfect_dain_1.text: *The gym. Dain fires off her last serve. Unwrapping her bandages.*

perfect_dain_2.name: Dain
perfect_dain_2.text: This is the last toss. — But it's also the start of something.

perfect_dain_2b.name: {name}
perfect_dain_2b.text: *No exclamation marks. For the first time. — Dain is talking about a beginning that isn't volleyball.*

perfect_dain_3.name: Dain
perfect_dain_3.text: Am I worth anything off the court too?

perfect_dain_3b.name: {name}
perfect_dain_3b.text: *Dain sets the volleyball down on the court. She turns around and smiles. A smile without exclamation marks.*

perfect_dain_4.name: {name}
perfect_dain_4.text: On the court and off it.

perfect_dain_5.name: {name}
perfect_dain_5.text: *Dain threw herself at me before I was ready. The volleyball rolled across the floor, and in the sunset-lit gym, only our two shadows remained.*

perfect_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_dain.text: *Dain's knee buckles as she lands from her jump. I know it hurts. But — she's smiling.*

perfect_epilogue_2_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_dain.text: *Dain became a sports commentator. She smiles in front of the camera. But this time it's a real smile.*

perfect_epilogue_3_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_3_dain.text: *Sometimes she says her knee hurts. Every time, I just sit beside her and say nothing. That's how we do it.*

bitter_dain_1.name: {name}
bitter_dain_1.text: *I confessed. Dain grinned and said she was happy. But that grin was the same kind she always wore. — About a month later, I got a text asking to meet in front of the gym.*

bitter_dain_2.name: Dain
bitter_dain_2.text: It really was fun! ...But I think fun was all it was. Kind of sad, huh.

bitter_dain_3.name: {name}
bitter_dain_3.text: *I left the gym. It's raining. — The exclamation marks came back, but the last sentence ended with a period.*

bitter_dain_3_b.name: {name}
bitter_dain_3_b.text: *I walked out past the school gate. It's raining. — No umbrella. Cherry blossoms stick to the wet ground at my feet.*

bitter_epilogue_1.name: {name}
bitter_epilogue_1.text: *After graduation, we heard from each other less and less. Once a month became once every two months, leaving each other on read became normal, and one day - when I opened the chat and had nothing to say - I knew it was over.*

bitter_epilogue_2.name: {name}
bitter_epilogue_2.text: *The record of five days remains. It doesn't hurt. It just — wasn't enough. For either of us.*

true_dain_1.name: {name}
true_dain_1.text: *The gym. The same emergency lights as yesterday. Lying side by side on the mat.*

true_dain_2.name: {name}
true_dain_2.text: *Dain grabs my hand, pulls it over, and presses it to the left side of her chest. Without a word.*

true_dain_2b.name: {name}
true_dain_2b.text: *Fast. A speed that needs no words.*

true_dain_3.name: {name}
true_dain_3.text: *The heartbeat under my fingertips is vivid.*

true_dain_4.name: {name}
true_dain_4.text: *The words don't come. My lips part slightly and stay there.*

true_dain_6.name: Dain
true_dain_6.text: *half hiding her face behind the volleyball* Why are you looking at me like that...? That's not fair.

true_dain_8.name: Dain
true_dain_8.text: You SO were!! ...But you can keep looking.

true_dain_8b.name: {name}
true_dain_8b.text: *The exclamation mark is back. — But this time, it's a real one.*

true_dain_bridge.name: {name}
true_dain_bridge.text: *Dain's laughter still lingers in my ears.*

true_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_dain.text: *It was five days. Five days to hear the heart hiding behind Dain's exclamation marks.*

true_epilogue_2.name: {name}
true_epilogue_2.text: *The uniform was stiff, the cherry blossoms made me sneeze, and I had no idea what to do in front of the school gate.*

true_epilogue_3.name: {name}
true_epilogue_3.text: *But looking back — I think it was already decided the moment our eyes first met. It just took five days to admit it.*

true_epilogue_4_seo.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_seo.text: *Her family hasn't gotten warmer. Her mother's calls are still cold, and the rehearsed smiles in front of the mirror haven't stopped. — But now she has someone she can show the face she never practiced.*

true_epilogue_4_yuna.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_yuna.text: *The person who disappeared still hasn't come back. The senior's number is still gone, and the corner seat in the library is still empty. But now she has someone she can speak to in her own voice, not just through notes.*

true_epilogue_4_dain.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_dain.text: *Her knee still isn't better. She still wraps it every morning, and her alarm note still has two exclamation marks. — But now she has someone who stays when her sentences end with a period.*

day5_ending_alone.name: {name}
day5_ending_alone.text: *I walk out the school gate. My phone buzzes. — Nobody. Low battery warning.*

alone_1.name: {name}
alone_1.text: *Five days. I reached out to people, failed to reach others, and in the end couldn’t choose anyone.*

alone_2.name: {name}
alone_2.text: *At my old school, I regretted not speaking up. At this school — do I regret not finding anyone? No. I found them but couldn’t choose. No — I didn’t have the courage to choose.*

alone_2_b.name: {name}
alone_2_b.text: *The room is eerily quiet. The voices that were still ringing in my ears fade with the click of the door. Cherry blossoms fall outside the window. The same ones that brushed my nose five days ago are now scattering in the wind.*

alone_4.name: {name}
alone_4.text: *...Being alone isn't a punishment. It's just quiet. Quieter than I expected.*

day5_ending_good.name: {name}
day5_ending_good.text: *Just saying 'I like you' didn't magically fix everything. Even so, we chose not to end it here.*

good_1.name: {name}
good_1.text: *We were clumsy, late, and missed each other more than once.*

good_1b.name: {name}
good_1b.text: *Still, this time we're facing the same direction.*

good_1c.name: {name}
good_1c.text: *It may not be a perfect happy ending, but from here, we can start again.*

good_1_seo.name: Seoyeon
good_1_seo.text: It won't be perfect. Not for you, not for me. ...But this time, don't let go halfway.

good_1_seo_b.name: {name}
good_1_seo_b.text: *Seoyeon brushes at the end of my sleeve the way she'd flick off a cherry blossom petal. It's a brusque touch, but not one that pushes me away.*

good_1_seo_c.name: {name}
good_1_seo_c.text: *Her words are short, but our steps fall into sync. For today, that feels like enough.*

good_1_seo_d.name: {name}
good_1_seo_d.text: *What Seoyeon and I have is only just beginning to take shape. Unsteady, but not broken.*

good_2_seo.name: {name}
good_2_seo.text: *At the end of the cherry blossom path, Seoyeon stops half a step ahead of me. When she looks back, her gaze is softer than it used to be.*

good_3_seo.name: {name}
good_3_seo.text: *"...Why aren't you coming?" She mutters it under her breath, but her slowed steps give her away — she was waiting.*

good_4_seo.name: {name}
good_4_seo.text: *I smiled, and Seoyeon pretended not to notice before the corner of her mouth lifted just a little.*

good_5_seo.name: {name}
good_5_seo.text: *As we walked slowly past the end of the cherry blossom path, I found myself thinking I wanted to walk this road with her next spring too. This time, I could say that out loud.*

good_epilogue_1.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1.text: *A text from Seoyeon. 'I made you a copy of the rooftop key. It's official, so don't worry.' She could've just called it an invitation.*

good_epilogue_2.name: {name}
good_epilogue_2.text: *Even at the very end, she acts nonchalant — and gives her heart by handing over a key.*

good_epilogue_3.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3.text: *I slip the key into my pocket. Tomorrow on the rooftop — this time it's my turn to pack the lunch.*

good_1_yuna.name: Yuna
good_1_yuna.text: ...You were late. Still — this time I read your sentence all the way to the end.

good_1_yuna_b.name: {name}
good_1_yuna_b.text: *Yuna hands me a folded note. When I open it, there's just one line: 'Next time, don't disappear.'*

good_1_yuna_b_b.name: {name}
good_1_yuna_b_b.text: *It's a short sentence, but this time it reads like a request.*

good_2_yuna.name: {name}
good_2_yuna.text: *The rooftop. Yuna leans against the railing. Even with the wind blowing, she doesn't turn away first today.*

good_3_yuna.name: {name}
good_3_yuna.text: *We look at the same sky. She doesn't say much, but the silence isn't cold the way it used to be.*

good_4_yuna.name: {name}
good_4_yuna.text: *I want to be remembered not as a stand-in, but as the person standing here right now. And I think Yuna wants the same.*

good_5_yuna.name: {name}
good_5_yuna.text: *Even as we left the rooftop and headed down the stairs, I felt the same. It's okay if it takes more time. This time, I want to read it through to the end and say everything through to the end.*

good_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *A folded note falls out of my bag. No idea when she slipped it in. 'If you finished volume 1, I'll lend you volume 2. — Yuna'*

good_epilogue_2_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_2_yuna.text: *Instead of words, Yuna prepares what comes next. Volume 2 after volume 1. Tomorrow after today. This is her version of 'let's keep meeting.'*

good_epilogue_3_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3_yuna.text: *On the back of the note, in small writing: '...Let's read the ending together.' The pale violet ink is smeared.*

good_1_dain.name: Dain
good_1_dain.text: Hey, it's true I'm not completely over it yet. ...But I'm at least at the point where I can throw you the ball again.

good_2_dain.name: {name}
good_2_dain.text: *In front of the school gate, Dain bounces the volleyball once and, this time without joking around, tosses it my way.*

good_3_dain.name: {name}
good_3_dain.text: *I catch it. Only then does Dain smile. Making up always looks like this with her.*

good_4_dain.name: {name}
good_4_dain.text: *Her knee still hurts, and neither of us has sorted everything out completely. Even so, we can still try running side by side.*

good_5_dain.name: {name}
good_5_dain.text: *As we walked out past the school gate together, it felt like the last serve had already crossed over. Now it's my turn to receive it.*

good_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1_dain.text: *A message from Dain. 'Anyone wanna work out tomorrow morning?' There's a question mark at the end. Normally it'd be an exclamation point.*

good_epilogue_2_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_2_dain.text: *For the first time, she cared about being turned down. When Dain uses a question mark — that's courage.*

good_epilogue_3_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3_dain.text: *I texted back. 'Deal.' No exclamation mark. I'll show up in person tomorrow instead.*

day5_ending_confess_fail.name: {name}
day5_ending_confess_fail.text: *I told them. I said it. — But what came back was silence.*

confess_fail_1.name: {name}
confess_fail_1.text: *Even after I walked away, those words still rang in my ears. "...Thank you. Really. But I'm not there yet — I guess five days was just too short."*

confess_fail_2.name: {name}
confess_fail_2.text: *It's not rejection. It's timing. — The result of five days that weren't enough to get close.*

confess_fail_3.name: {name}
confess_fail_3.text: *My feelings weren't fake. We just still knew too little about each other for them to truly land.*

confess_fail_4.name: {name}
confess_fail_4.text: *One thing makes this failure different from before. At least this time I said it, and that means I can truly let it end.*

day5_ending_friend.name: {name}
day5_ending_friend.text: *In the end, I couldn't say it.*

friend_1.name: {name}
friend_1.text: *The cherry blossoms are being blown away by the wind.*

friend_2.name: {name}
friend_2.text: *Same thing I did at my old school. I did it again.*

friend_3.name: {name}
friend_3.text: *There definitely were moments when I could have said I liked her. But once again, I chose the safe way out.*

friend_4.name: {name}
friend_4.text: *As I leave the school gate, a message comes in. 'Thanks for today lol.' — It's easy, familiar. That makes it feel even more like friendship.*

friend_4_seo.name: {name}
friend_4_seo.text: *As I leave the school gate, a message comes in. 'Thanks to you, today was less awkward. Get home safe.' Kind, but airtight. It's exactly the tone of someone drawing a line and staying behind it.*

friend_4_yuna.name: {name}
friend_4_yuna.text: *As I leave the school gate, a message comes in. '...Thanks. For today.' It's short. There's a period at the end. A line that would've thrilled me before now feels like a boundary.*

friend_4_dain.name: {name}
friend_4_dain.text: *As I leave the school gate, a message comes in. 'Hey, get home safe! Thanks for today!' The exclamation marks are back. That's a relief — but my mood sinks even more. They're the kind you send a friend.*

friend_5.name: {name}
friend_5.text: *I text back. 'Me too, thanks.' — Then stare at the screen. Two short lines. I'm smiling, but it doesn't feel good at all.*

friend_7.name: {name}
friend_7.text: *...I couldn’t say it at this school either.*

friend_8.name: {name}
friend_8.text: *Graduation day. Scrolling through my phone gallery. Where Sojeong's photo used to be three years ago, there's now a group photo with friends from this school. I'm turning my head away — just like I did back then.*

friend_9.name: {name}
friend_9.text: *Once again, I'm standing next to that person, wearing my easiest expression and smiling like just a friend.*

friend_10.name: {name}
friend_10.text: *I open the notes app. ‘I need to tell you something.’ — The cursor blinks. Just like three years ago. I hold down backspace and erase the words.*

day5_ending_mayhem.name: {name}
day5_ending_mayhem.text: *I liked all three of them. Genuinely. — And that’s why I couldn’t choose anyone.*

mayhem_1.name: {name}
mayhem_1.text: *Seoyeon brushed past me in the hallway. She didn't turn her head. — Of course.*

mayhem_2.name: {name}
mayhem_2.text: *Yuna’s seat was empty. A single note on the desk. ‘It was fun.’ The period was the end.*

mayhem_3.name: {name}
mayhem_3.text: *Dain was smiling. Bright as always. — But the exclamation marks were gone. Take care. The first time I ever heard Dain end a sentence with a period — and of all things, it was a farewell.*

mayhem_4.name: {name}
mayhem_4.text: *I watched all three walk away. None of them looked back. — That was the answer.*

mayhem_5.name: {name}
mayhem_5.text: *Spring is ending. The cherry blossoms are falling. No one is by my side.*

mayhem_6.name: {name}
mayhem_6.text: *I learned too late that saying I liked them wasn't enough to protect anything.*

mayhem_7.name: {name}
mayhem_7.text: *With Sojeong, I stayed silent and lost one person. This time I spoke to everyone and lost everyone. — Same result in the end. I couldn't say it right.*

day5_ending_harem.name: {name}
day5_ending_harem.text: *I like all of you. — When those words left my mouth, all three faces froze at once.*

harem_1.name: {name}
harem_1.text: *Seoyeon smiled first. ...Fine. At least you’re honest. It wasn’t my imagination that I heard teeth grinding behind that smile.*

harem_1_b.name: {name}
harem_1_b.text: *Yuna lowered her head. When she looked up a long time later, she was smiling — the kind of smile that's too broken to cry. Biting her lip.*

harem_3.name: {name}
harem_3.text: *Dain punched my shoulder with her fist. It hurt. Are you insane? ...But I fell for you knowing you’re like that, so that’s on me. Hmph.*

harem_4.name: {name}
harem_4.text: *Monday is Seoyeon. Wednesday is Yuna. Friday is Dain. My phone calendar is a minefield. Call Wednesday's name on Monday and it's all over.*

harem_5.name: {name}
harem_5.text: *When Seoyeon asked, "What are you doing on Wednesday?" my heart nearly stopped. Wednesday is Yuna's day.*

harem_6.name: {name}
harem_6.text: *And still, all three of them are smiling today. Even knowing what tomorrow looks like, I reach for today again.*

harem_7.name: {name}
harem_7.text: *Three alarms, three personas, three lies. — To call this happiness, the knots in my stomach come far too often.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_1.text: *Graduation is over. I'm alone in the empty classroom. The chalk marks on the blackboard haven't been erased yet.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_1b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_1b.text: *The door opens. — It's her. Beige cardigan. Holding a document envelope.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2.text: Congratulations on graduating. ...The paperwork's all done. My job as your teacher is finished now.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2b.text: Is the manuscript still in your desk drawer?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2c.text: *She pauses. About to say something more, then closes her mouth.* ...Take care.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3b.text: *Cafe terrace. Cherry blossoms drift through the air. As I step in - I see someone familiar at the window seat.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3c.text: ...Oh. I'm surprised too. *She sets down her coffee cup.* Want to sit?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3e.text: *She smirks.* Quit teaching. Just writing now. Part-time at a cafe too. — What about you?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3f.text: ...Can we meet again? I come here every Thursday.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3g.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3g.text: *That 'next time' became the time after, and the time after that. Same seat every Thursday. When the barista asked 'Couple's table?', neither of us could answer. Then one Thursday, we walked the streets instead of the cafe. Side by side. Both pretending not to notice our shadows overlapping.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4b.text: *She stops suddenly at the bookstore.* ...I finished my manuscript. Want to read it?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4c.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4c.text: *I went home and read the manuscript. All night. — The main character's offhand lines kept sounding strangely familiar.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4d.text: *Next Thursday, at the café. She stirred her coffee longer than usual.* ...How was it?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4e.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4e.text: *Next Thursday. I didn't wait outside the cafe. — I waited outside the flower shop.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4f.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4f.text: *I handed her the bouquet.* This isn't professional interest. Not on my end.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4g.text: *She takes the bouquet and stares at it for a long time. Her hands tremble. — She smiles.* ...Me neither.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_5.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_5.text: *This is a secret. Just ours. — This bouquet weighs more than the diploma.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep1.text: *We didn't leave the café that day. Not until sunset. — All the words we couldn't say in that classroom four years ago came pouring out.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep2.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep2.text: *Thursday's café became our café. The staff stopped asking 'couple's seat?' They just show us to our table.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep3.text: *The manuscript was published. No name in the dedication. Just one line: 'Three pages of feedback from the teacher's desk drawer — that's where this story began.'*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep4.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep4.text: *Sometimes she says 'I used to be your teacher' and I reply 'I used to be your student.' We both laugh. — Because now we're just two people.*

hidden_true_homeroom_1.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_1.text: *Graduation day. — Time has passed. The uniform isn't stiff anymore.*

hidden_true_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_2.text: *An empty classroom. The same classroom where she used to write. — My homeroom teacher is waiting.*

hidden_true_homeroom_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_2_b.text: *She's leaning by the window at the back of the classroom. No lessons, no duties — just her face.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_4_b.text: *It was unconscious. — The moment I graduated, the title fell away.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_4_c.text: *She pulls out an envelope. This time it's not brown — it's white.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_d.text: I finished the manuscript. — I could write it because you were my first reader.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_f.text: I asked for one line and you wrote three pages. After seeing that, I had no more excuses to postpone it.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_g.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_4_g.text: *She looks out the window. Cherry blossoms are falling.*

hidden_true_homeroom_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_5.text: *Looking out the window* ...So. Since I finished it, I'm thinking about sending it to a publisher. — What do you think?

hidden_true_homeroom_5_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_5_c.text: *The uniform isn't stiff anymore. No — today is the day I take it off.*

hidden_true_homeroom_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_6.text: ...Just one thing. ...Let's go get coffee. Real coffee this time, not juice.

hidden_true_homeroom_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_6_b.text: *From juice to coffee. — From student to adult. Not crossing the line — the line itself disappeared.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_7_b.text: *She smiles. Not a dry one — the smile of someone who finished a seven-year unfinished manuscript.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_7_c.text: ...I really shouldn't be doing this. *— Her voice trails off. Then she smiles.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_7_d.text: *One last time. Then the habit breaks. — Seven years of 'teacher' are over, and the day to call her by name has come.*

hidden_true_homeroom_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_8.text: ...But even though I shouldn't be doing this — I don't regret it.

hidden_good_homeroom_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_good_homeroom_1.text: *She was waiting in front of the school.* Congratulations on graduating.

hidden_good_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_2.text: *During the handshake — something slips into my palm. A folded note.*

hidden_good_homeroom_3.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_3.text: *Leaving the school. 'When I finish the manuscript, I'll reach out. Because I want to show it to you first.' There's a phone number.*

hidden_good_homeroom_4.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_4.text: *Her hand held on about three seconds longer than a handshake should. Too long for a handshake, too short for a confession.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_1.text: *Graduation was over. I opened the nurse's office door. It was empty. A single bandage sat on the desk. 'Come to my place. Address on the back.' No heart this time.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_2.text: *The person who opens the door looks far more at ease than she ever did in the infirmary.* ...You came. I didn't think you really would.

hidden_perfect_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_3.text: *Side by side on the living room couch. The sun is setting outside the window. Instead of a bandage, fingers are touching.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_3b.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_3b.text: *She leans against me.* ...I don't need excuses anymore. Not a patient, not a student.

hidden_perfect_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_4.text: *Her hand reaches up and takes my tie. She doesn't let go.* ...I'm not sending you home tonight.

hidden_perfect_nurse_4b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_4b.text: *Morning. Light seeping through the curtains. Breathing beside me. — The person who used to take three minutes to put on a bandage is now asleep holding my hand.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_5.text: *She opens her eyes. Smiles.* ...Does it hurt anywhere? Want me to take a look? *— Not a joke. Not this time.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_5b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_5b.text: *Just — someone I want to be with. Right here.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep1.text: *Morning. A bandage stuck to the kitchen table. Today's menu written on it. — Her version of a sticky note.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep2.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep2.text: *She went back to the university hospital. This time, the patients call her by name. — Nurse Lee Juwon.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep3.text: *The rosemary pot has been moved to the windowsill. To the sunny side. — She's watering it.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep4.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep4.text: *The light-green notebook has been tucked deep in the drawer. What's written on the last page isn't a letter — just one line: 'Yujin, I'm okay now.' — A period, three years in the making.*

hidden_true_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_1.text: *Graduation day. Walking out the school gate — there's a bandage stuck to the nurse's office door.*

hidden_true_nurse_2.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2.text: *'Congratulations on graduating. I'll wait at the cafe.' — When I peel off the bandage, there's a tiny map underneath. The school nurse is sitting in the cafe. She looks far more at ease than she ever did in the infirmary. Just — like someone who came to wait for me.*

hidden_true_nurse_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2_b.text: *Today, she looks more like just a person than a teacher.*

hidden_true_nurse_3.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_3.text: Congrats on graduating. Starting today, you can drop the 'teacher.'

hidden_true_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_4.text: You know... when you came to the nurse's office on your first day. You touched your forehead and asked if I could 'check your blood pressure that way.' I thought you were joking.

hidden_true_nurse_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5.text: ...But right now, I don't intend to gloss over it like that.

hidden_true_nurse_5_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_5_b.text: *Her voice dropped a register. All playfulness completely gone. — This is her sincerity.*

hidden_true_nurse_5_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_c.text: I knew it couldn't be, right? That's why I kept passing it off as a joke.

hidden_true_nurse_5_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_d.text: But you saw right through me, even when I was glossing things over.

hidden_true_nurse_5_e.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_5_e.text: Taking three minutes to put on a bandage isn't just being careful.

hidden_true_nurse_5_f.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_5_f.text: *The school nurse pauses. — Then smiles. Not a playful smile.*

hidden_true_nurse_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_6.text: So after the ceremony — come see me again. Not at the nurse's office. Here. And next time, I'll be just Juwon, not the school nurse.

hidden_true_nurse_7.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_7.text: *Even after we left the cafe, our hands didn't part easily. By the time I came to my senses, we were standing in front of her house, not the nurse's office.*

hidden_true_nurse_7_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_7_b.text: ...You're the first one who's seen right through me.

hidden_true_nurse_7_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_7_c.text: *The school nurse reaches out and touches the bandage on the back of my hand. The same one she put on this morning.*

hidden_true_nurse_7_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_7_d.text: *She was someone who needed an excuse. — Her role at school had been both her excuse and her wall. Today, that wall disappeared.*

hidden_true_nurse_8.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8.text: Now, don't pretend to be hurt just to come see me. Just say you wanted to see me.

hidden_true_nurse_8_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_b.text: *Turning her coffee cup in her hands* ...I never thought I'd miss the smell of the nurse's office after graduation.

hidden_true_nurse_8_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_c.text: *The day called graduation erased the line between us. A cafe instead of the nurse's office. A person instead of a role.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_d.text: *The school nurse looks at me. No playfulness.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_e.text: You know... back then, I was thinking about quitting.

hidden_true_nurse_8_g.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_g.text: But when you came — I had a reason to stay here. *Smiling softly* Thank you.

hidden_good_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2.text: Vitamins. — Take care of yourself in college. ...Medical concern. This time, for real.

hidden_good_nurse_2_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2_c.text: *Pausing briefly* ...Yes. Medical concern. *Quietly* This time, for real.

hidden_good_nurse_2_d.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_2_d.text: *'This time, for real.' — Meaning all the other times, it wasn't.*

hidden_good_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_3.text: *Leaving the nurse's office. Inside the bottle cap, tiny writing. 'Call me if you're sick. Call me even if you're not. — ♥'*

hidden_good_nurse_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_3_b.text: *Even after I close the cap, the corners of my mouth won't go down.*

hidden_good_nurse_4.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_4.text: *My hand holding the bottle stops. I think of the light-green notebook in the nurse's office drawer. Someday, I hope she can close the final page of that letter.*

perfect_epilogue_1b_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1b_dain.text: *Every morning wrapping bandages, secretly rubbing her knee when no one was looking. That person just jumped.*

perfect_epilogue_1c_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1c_dain.text: *If the reason she can jump despite the pain is me — that's enough.*
